[EveryCentsCount] I was with GloBird until yesterday, but I’ve just switched to CovaU and I think this type of plan makes more sense for households with a decent-sized solar + battery system.
If you have something like a 10kW solar system with a 42kWh battery, especially in summer, you don’t necessarily need free electricity hours because you’re already producing plenty of your own energy. The bigger thing for me is getting a reasonable feed-in tariff throughout the day.
One downside I found with GloBird is that they weren’t paying solar feed-in before 4pm, which can be a disadvantage in summer when your solar is producing heavily during the middle of the day.
With CovaU, I’m getting:
• 11am–2pm free electricity
• 5c/kWh feed-in during the day
• 15c/kWh feed-in from 6pm–9pm
• Around 16c/kWh off-peak from midnight–6am
For someone with a large solar + battery system, I think the 6–9pm 15c feed-in is particularly interesting because you can use the battery to export during that period rather than relying only on the free electricity window.
Obviously, everyone’s usage and solar setup is different, so what works for me may not necessarily work for someone else. But for my setup, I think this tariff structure is more suitable than what I was getting with GloBird.
[Weasel] The main difference is with Globird you receive the $1 credit for not using the grid between 6-8pm. You would need to feed in 6.6kw equivelent with CovaU during that same period. Ofcourse its all depends on each individual household usage for which plan is best.
My concern is CovaU reducing the feed in rates or raising the daily supply charge in the near future, just like FlowPower. Free usage is also capped at 50 kWh for free charge period, whereby Globird grandfathered plans are unlimited.
